claims.text: The starting material is a near-equiatomic alloy containing five or more metals.
The starting nanoparticles are crystalline solid solutions.
High-temperature annealing in a reducing atmosphere will introduce oxygen vacancies into the nanoparticles.
Oxygen vacancies will reduce lattice strain in the multielement metallic solid solution.
Oxygen vacancies will enhance cohesion between the constituent metal elements.
Reduced lattice strain and enhanced interelement cohesion will improve thermal stability and reduce degradation at 773–1173 K.
Vacancy-treated nanoparticles will be more stable than untreated nanoparticles during operation at 773–1173 K.
Vacancy-treated nanoparticles will exhibit better catalytic performance than untreated nanoparticles.
The proposed intervention is compatible with catalytic materials having low noble-metal content.
The intervention is expected to work for compositions capable of retaining a stable multielement solid solution.
The optimal vacancy concentration, vacancy distribution, reducing atmosphere, and annealing conditions remain to be determined experimentally.

contradictions.description: The initial material is specified as a metallic solid solution composed of metals, while the proposed mediator is an oxygen vacancy, which ordinarily presupposes an oxygen-containing lattice. No initial oxide, oxygen-bearing phase, surface oxide, or oxidation step is specified to reconcile these descriptions while retaining the claimed solid solution.
